RagShortTexts: The House of Sanseverino commanded Cilento and Salerno, serving as premier barons of the.

Variants.Content: The Sanseverino held the Salernitan plain and the Cilento hills, a country of olive terraces, coastal passes and mountain villages that resisted any centralised rule. Their claim to Norman descent and their office of Grand Constable gave them a place at the Sicilian court, but their real power rested on vast estates that fielded hundreds of heavy cavalry. As the Hohenstaufen dynasty entered its twilight, their retinues decided which side could hold the mountains and the coastal roads. Castles on the limestone crags controlled the passes between Salerno and the interior, so no army could move through the region without first buying or breaking the Sanseverino garrisons.

Manfred and any future Angevin claimant had to offer confirmations of fiefs, offices and tolls to the Sanseverino, because no prince could govern Naples in peace without this family's support. Letters passed between the Cilento lords and the Sicilian chancery, and every marriage or wardship settled was a move in the wider contest for the south.

Perched upon limestone crags in Cilento, the Sanseverino forts watch the coastal passes. Armoured retainers form up on narrow tracks where horses cannot wheel, and they fight with close shields and short swords. Rain turns the mountain roads to slurry, and a man who has marched all night still climbs the scree in his mail, because the next ambush always waits above the pass.
